title: Labour market mismatch: strong engineering and tech hiring demand alongside PMET retrenchments
asked: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye asked the Minister for Manpower what key factors are driving the mismatch between strong hiring demand for engineers and technology specialists and rising retrenchments among PMETs.
response: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong said mismatches may be driven by shifts in skill requirements: firms are expanding technology functions, sustaining demand for AI engineers and engineering professionals, while restructuring PMET roles that have become easier to automate, and retrenched PMETs may lack the specific technical skills for in-demand jobs. He said hiring demand for PMETs remains higher than PMET retrenchments, with finance and infocomm having 4,100 and 5,300 PMET vacancies as of December 2025 against 960 PMET retrenchments across both sectors in the last quarter of 2025. He said the Government will continue supporting workers to upskill and reskill, and that Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programmes provide salary support to employers, placing over 7,300 workers into tech and engineering related jobs over the last three years.
